notes: Abstract. Both concrete overrides (MouseInputTracker, MouseWheelInputTracker) return `(anInt7432/anInt7419 and 0x2) != 0`, checking bit 1 of the latched-button bitmask assembled from AWT modifiers in each subclass's private button-decode helper (BUTTON1=bit0/left, BUTTON2=bit1/middle, BUTTON3=bit2/right - confirmed via MouseInputTracker.method3604 which maps java.awt old-style modifier masks 0x10/0x8/0x4 to return codes 1/2/4). Param unused in both overrides (only feeds a dead modulo expression in MouseInputTracker and a discarded comparison in MouseWheelInputTracker).

Abstract 'advance one tick' method. Both overrides copy the accumulated button-mask/x/y into the double-buffered 'current frame' fields; MouseInputTracker always swaps its queued-event NodeDeque pair, MouseWheelInputTracker only swaps when `tickFlag==0`. Called exactly once per client tick from Client.kt (`aInputTracker_8552.method3589(0)`).
Abstract. Both overrides return `(anInt7432/anInt7419 and 0x4) != 0` - the right/BUTTON3 bit of the latched button mask (see method3588 notes on the bit layout). Param unused in both overrides.

Abstract 'detach from AWT component' method. MouseInputTracker unconditionally removes its mouse/motion listeners and nulls its queues regardless of `i`, plus a dead `method3597(false)` side-call when `i!=0` (only observed call site, NpcReference.kt, passes 0, so that branch never fires). MouseWheelInputTracker only detaches when `i==0` (same observed value at the only call site).

Concrete (base class, not overridden). Returns `isLeftButtonDown() || isMiddleButtonDown() || isRightButtonDown()` (see method3595/method3588/method3590). Self-recursive dead branch `if (i <= 91) method3593(53)` whose return value is discarded. Only call site (DragDropController.kt, `method3593(94)`) passes 94 (>91), so the recursive branch never fires there - kept as a real-looking guard rather than a confirmed decoy since only one call site was observed.

Abstract getter for the latched mouse Y coordinate (`anInt7448` in MouseInputTracker / `anInt7416` in MouseWheelInputTracker). Always called paired with method3597 (X) across the renderer (Client.kt, ChatCommandProcessor.kt, DragDropController.kt, FlipTextureNode.kt, FloatGrid.kt, GlArrayBufferObject.kt, HudTabPanel.kt, NpcDefinitionCache.kt, ScriptCompilerThread.kt) to read the current mouse position. Byte param is a decoy guard in both overrides - the threshold checks (`i<=69`/`i<69`) are never true at any real call site, which all pass positive bytes in the 70-127 range.

Abstract. Both overrides return `(anInt7432/anInt7419 and 0x1) != 0` - the BUTTON1/left bit of the latched mask. Param unused in both overrides (only feeds a dead re-entrant `mouseExited`/`mouseMoved` call whose result is discarded).

Abstract. Both overrides dequeue the next `TimedRecordAccessor` from the 'ready' NodeDeque populated by the AWT mouse listener callbacks (i.e. pop the next buffered click/drag/wheel event). Consumed by Client.kt's main input-processing loop, which calls it repeatedly until it returns null.

Abstract getter for the latched mouse X coordinate (`anInt7442` in MouseInputTracker / `anInt7417` in MouseWheelInputTracker). See method3594 (Y) - always called in pairs across the renderer. Boolean param is a decoy in both overrides: MouseInputTracker's `if (bool != true) anInt7453 = -101` and MouseWheelInputTracker's `if (bool != true) return 27` are both dead since every real call site passes `true`.
